chunks.title: Origin of information
chunks.text: There's a number of places information can come from. Let's step through a few of these sort of from most public to least public. But even this is certainly not an exhaustive list. There's many other places we can get information. But let's step through them.

chunks.title: Origin of information
chunks.text: Price volume. This is public. It's rapid. It's quick. Everybody can see it.

chunks.title: Origin of information
chunks.text: This is the basis of technical analysis. Fundamental data. This is reported quarterly. And everybody can see it as well. It's public.

chunks.title: Origin of information
chunks.text: But it points more to the root of the value of the company than just the price volume. Exogenous data, it's a fancy name for a simple concept. It's just information about the world that affects the company. As an example, if we were looking at an airline stock, an exogenous piece of data that would affect the price of the airline stock is the price of oil.

chunks.title: Origin of information
chunks.text: If the price of oil goes down, usually the price of the airline stock goes up. Because energy is the number one cost for airlines. A very important and secretive type of information relates to company insiders. So let's suppose you're a CEO and you know that this drug that you've invented is about to be improved.

chunks.title: Origin of information
chunks.text: You might go buy shares of your stock because you think the price of your stock is going to go up because that drug is going to be approved. Now depending on the circumstance, it may or may not be legal. But this reflects information that you have that people outside the company do not have. And so this insider information is probably the least accessible of all these types, of course,

chunks.title: Origin of information
chunks.text: and of most other types of information as well. Now each of these types of information has a relationship to the efficient markets hypothesis. In particular, there's three forms of the efficient markets hypothesis. And these types of information relate to each of these three forms. We'll get into that in just a second.
